messages:
maya: heads-up — after landing raster-tiling-v2 on perf-cluster we see a 7-12% tail-latency regression on long-seq workloads. repro is stable on flavor-gpu-a. I suspect an interaction between the new tiling pipeline and paged-attn kernel selection; KV cache hit rate dipped slightly too.

maya: reproducer: seq=2048 batch=1 model=decoder-only; baseline (flashq-unfused): p50=45ms p95=120ms p99=210ms tokens/s=1800; after change: p50=48ms p95=135ms p99=260ms tokens/s=1600. global mem BW 92% -> 98%. KV hit rate -0.6%.

tom: ack. can you paste the kernel-selector logs and the lightweight perf profile?

maya: selector log snippet: 
```
[2026-03-16T17:12:10Z] policy: latency-preferred
[info] candidate_kernels: [flash_paged_fused_v3, flash_paged_unfused_v2, flash_unfused]
[info] selected_kernel: flash_paged_fused_v3
[reason] smem_fit=true, occupancy=0.78, expected_seq=1024, seq=2048 -> heuristic favored fused for cache locality
```
profile sample (nvprof-like):
```
GPU memory BW: 98% peak
SM utilization: 92%
L2 bw: high
DRAM writes: +18% vs baseline
KV cache misses: +0.6% absolute
```

sophia: wow, DRAM writes +18% is suspicious — fused path may be doing extra partial writes to global memory because of the paged-kv spill path. Did we change the pipeline stage ordering in raster-tiling-v2?

maya: yes, raster-tiling-v2 reorders stage 2/3 to improve occupancy for short sequences. That helped p50 on small seq, but looks like it increases sync points for long sequences which triggers extra global flushes in the fused paged path.

lin: hypothesis: when fused paged kernel runs with pipeline-stage-order B->A we get extra bank-conflict-causing stores. microbench idea: run kernel microbench across seqs and measure sharedmem bank-conflict counts + bbw. Try: `./bench_kernel --model=flash_paged_fused_v3 --seq=512,1024,1536,2048 --iters=200 --perf-counters`

maya: ran it. results:
```
bench flash_paged_fused_v3 seq=1024: mean=32.2ms, bw=91%, bank_conflicts=420
bench flash_paged_unfused_v2 seq=1024: mean=30.8ms, bw=78%, bank_conflicts=60
bench flash_unfused seq=1024: mean=31.0ms, bw=76%, bank_conflicts=58

bench flash_paged_fused_v3 seq=2048: mean=64.8ms, bw=98%, bank_conflicts=1100
bench flash_paged_unfused_v2 seq=2048: mean=60.2ms, bw=81%, bank_conflicts=140
```

maya: so fused paged variant shows much higher bank_conflicts and BW for long seq — looks like tiling interacts badly and causes many partial per-tile writes.

aaron: concrete mitigation options:
- short-term: kernel-selector tweak to prefer flash_paged_unfused_v2 for seq >= 1536 or when sharedmem_bw > 90%
- medium: add a quick patch to fused kernel to reduce intermediate global writes (avoid per-tile flush if smem can hold KV chunk)
- long-term: refine allocator to prefer different block sizes for paged kv with raster-tiling-v2

tom: +1 for selector fallback as a canary. less risky than reverting whole tiling change. we can gate it behind perf-flag and run canary for 24h.

maya: opened PR #3248 with selector rule: `if seq >= 1536 || smem_bw>0.9 -> prefer flash_paged_unfused_v2`. CI perf-run attached.

ci-bot: perf-run summary: canary rollout of selector-rule on perf-cluster-2: p99 reduced from 260ms -> 220ms (measured on 1k runs, 95% CI). tokens/s recovered ~ +8%. KV miss delta neutralized. Link: https://ci.internal/perf/3248

sophia: nice. let's keep that as temporary workaround. please also add a unit test that simulates paged kv with large seq so selector doesn't regress again.

lin: would still like to follow-up on fused kernel fix — I can prototype a smem-first spill to avoid global writes. will bench after PR lands.

maya: thanks all — rolling canary now. will update thread if we see any unexpected regressions. :thumbsup:
